title: SLO tacit knowledge transfer checklist and ops script
body:
Purpose
This is a working checklist + lightweight ops script intended to capture tacit knowledge for operationalizing SLOs across teams. The doc focuses on the communication patterns, decision scripts for common SLO lifecycle events, and a compact handoff checklist for when a feature team or platform team moves an SLO from trial -> adopted. Aim: reduce friction during handoffs and make critical decisions repeatable without heavy coordination.

Audience
Primary: on-call SREs, feature team leads, platform engineers, reliability liaisons. Secondary: product managers, support leads, solutions engineers who need to understand escalation flows.

Scope and constraints
- Scope: SLO adoption handoffs, incident-to-SLO feedback loops, change communication, and post-adoption run cadence.
- Not scope: deep technical runbooks for specific services (those live in service runbooks).
- Constraint: This doc should be consumable in a single 30–45 minute read and used as chemistry for a 1-hour handoff meeting.

Goals
1) Provide a minimal checklist so teams can declare an SLO "ready for adoption."
2) Surface the communication templates (email/Slack/confluence) for changes to SLO thresholds, burn pacing, and ownership.
3) Define a short decision script for when to revert an SLO change or open a remediation sprint.
4) Capture the tacit heuristics (what to look at in telemetry, quick triage questions).

Definitions (quick)
- Adoption: SLO is monitored by SRE and included in monthly reliability report, oncall playbook references it, and there is a named steward.
- Steward: person responsible for coordinating SLO improvements and communicating customer impact.

Minimal pre-adoption checklist (feature team)
- [ ] SLO definition written (objective, window, metric, golden tags). Link to draft: Confluence + saved Grafana panel.
- [ ] Owner/steward assigned (name + backup).
- [ ] Alerting baseline created: one symptomatic alert (burn > X%) and one signal alert (metric gap).
- [ ] Load/latency/quality baseline observed for >= 14 days. Attach tokenized example traces.
- [ ] Runbook stub created with expected mitigation steps and links to rollback patches.
- [ ] Postmortem incident pattern analysis (if there were outages in the last 90d) attached.
- [ ] Canary or staged rollout plan exists that respects SLO windows.

Adoption handoff script (30–45 minute meeting)
1) 5m TLDR by feature lead: what the SLO is, why it matters, target launch date.
2) 5m Data snapshot: traffic shape, peak percentiles, expected seasonality.
3) 10m Alerts and mitigations: show alerts, escalation steps, who gets paged.
4) 10m Operational scenarios: two failure scenarios (fast spike, slow drift) and demo mitigations.
5) 5m Canary/rollback plan and gating.
6) 5m Open decisions and action owners.
Deliverable: checkboxes above updated, owner accepts steward role, SRE schedules a 30-day follow-up review.

Communication patterns (templates + rules of thumb)
- Slack-first for immediate ops chatter (channel: #sre-service-<service>) with a short summary and link to runbook. Use thread for decisions.
- Email/Confluence update for non-urgent SLO policy changes (48–72h heads-up + scheduled Q&A).
- Pager duty message must include: metric, window, current burn rate, trigger timestamp, and mitigation attempt.

Suggested Slack message (incident to SLO)
- Title: [Page] <service> SLO burn 15m > 200%
- Body: quick bullets: metric, observed value, most likely cause hypothesis, immediate mitigation attempted, owner. Link to Grafana + runbook.

When to open a remediation sprint (decision script)
1) If burn persists > 2x target for 48 hours without clear mitigation -> open remediation sprint.
2) If customer-impacting errors correlate with SLO degradation -> immediate sprint.
3) If burn rate spikes but remediations reduce it within expected window -> work with steward, no sprint.
Note: We prefer short, time-boxed remediation sprints (1–2 weeks) focused on observability + quick fallbacks before large-scope refactors.

Triage heuristics (tacit heuristics to check quickly)
- Check service-level percentiles (p50/p95/p99) and rate-normalized error counts.
- Look for upstream dependency regressions (deploys, traffic shifts).
- Compare recent releases: any feature flags toggled?
- Confirm alert fidelity: do synthetic checks align with real-user metrics?

Post-adoption cadence (recommended)
- 7d: SRE-led health check (first week after adoption) — confirm alerts, noisy signals removed.
- 30d: adoption review — burn across window, false positive rate of alerts, steward retrospectives.
- Monthly: SLO health report included in reliability deck.
- Quarterly: readiness review for capacity and threshold drift.

Quick runbook skeleton (to be copied into service runbook)
- Title: <service>: SLO <name> (objective: 99.5% 30d)
- Symptoms: short bullets of how the degradation shows up in UX or logs.
- First responders: list names, Slack handles, pagers.
- First 10 minutes: quick checks and mitigations.
- 30–90 minute play: fallback modes, rollbacks, throttles, circuit breakers.
- When to escalate to SE/Platform/Network.
- Post-incident: short checklist for evidence capture and follow-up owner.

Example handoff notes (short, realistic example)
- Service: embeddings-indexer
- SLO: index-persist-success-rate >= 99.9% over 7d window
- Steward: Priya Kapoor, backup: Diego Morales
- Alerts: burn > 1% over baseline for 1h (symptomatic), success-rate drop < 99.7% (signal)
- Known risk: upstream storage throttling during region maintenance windows.
- Canary plan: 2% traffic for 24h -> 10% for 72h -> full traffic with monitor gates.
- Go/no-go owner: Priya (steward) + oncall SRE assigned at adoption.

Open decisions to resolve before adoption
- Should synthetic checks live in the control plane or service-owned Grafana? (Options and tradeoffs listed in team thread).
- Final threshold for p99 latency (data collection ongoing).
- Who owns the scheduled monthly reliability slide? (ops or product?)

Artifacts to attach for adoption ticket
- Grafana panel snapshot (png) and link.
- Raw export of 30-day metric window (CSV).
- Runbook link.
- Test/canary deployment plan and expected metrics.

Appendix: small templates
- 48h SLO-change announcement (Confluence): Summary, rationale, metric, expected impact, rollback plan, Q&A session link.
- 1-hour incident channel opener: short bullets + quick commands to run (curl mocks, debug endpoints).

Notes to self / followups (working list)
- Build a tiny UI checklist in console for handoff (parking idea).
- Add a short recording template for the adoption meeting (5 minute data walkthrough).
- Run a pilot with embeddings-indexer and search-reads next sprint.

Revision history
- 2027-03-15 Ava Chen: created initial draft with checklist and handoff script.
- 2027-04-10 Diego Morales: added triage heuristics and remediation decision script.
- 2027-05-02 Priya Kapoor: added example and open decisions section.
- 2027-06-10 Maya Singh: updated cadence and artifacts list; preparing for review.

End of document
